aggressive_definition: Incident lethal prostate cancer, defined as metastatic or fatal prostate cancer, among initially cancer-free men.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: It is unknown whether alcohol intake is associated with the risk of lethal (metastatic or fatal) prostate cancer.
study_design: Prospective cohort study with a separate incident lethal prostate cancer analysis among cancer-free men and postdiagnosis progression and mortality analyses among men with nonmetastatic prostate cancer.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Our analysis of alcohol intake among men at risk of prostate cancer included 47,568 cancer-free men.
reason: The abstract explicitly evaluates incident lethal prostate cancer among cancer-free men. It also reports postdiagnosis progression and mortality analyses, but those are not incident cancer endpoints. No total/general incident prostate cancer association is reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Alcohol drinkers had a lower risk of lethal prostate cancer (any v none: HR, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.71 to 0.99]) without a dose-response relationship.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns lethal prostate cancer among the 47,568 cancer-free men, so it is an aggressive incident endpoint rather than postdiagnosis progression or survival.
